items.title: [Performance][NIXL] BLHNC MLA caches lost whole-row registration in #53781 and now need more NIXL descriptors than LBHNC
items.author: stu-cao
items.body_excerpt:
## Your current environment
- GLM-5.3 (78 MLA + 21 indexer layers) with a DFlash2 draft (6 layers, GQA, 8 KV heads, fp8 KV, k=4).
- Prefill DEP8 (TP1 per rank). Decode TP4. Pull-mode `NixlConnector`, GPU-resident KV (no host buffer).
- vLLM main @ `4e0a414c44`, plus #58471 (GQA draft head slicing under an MLA target), the NVFP4
  prefill-context gather from #58744, and our NVFP4 KV decode path (`nvfp4_ds_mla` on
  `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, #59342).
- GB200 NVL72 (NIXL over NVLink), and B300 HGX (NIXL over RDMA).

## Describe the issue

### 1. Whole-row transfer is unreachable for page-contiguous BLHNC MLA caches
#53781 (HiSparse host-resident hot-buffering) put `not page_contiguous` in front of the
"packed MLA layouts transfer the complete storage row" branch of
`NixlConnectorWorker.register_kv_caches`:

```python
# before #53781
elif storage_is_block_major and (
    (packed_storage and is_mla_region)
    or (not hnc_contiguous and not self._is_csa_linear)
):
# after #53781
elif storage_is_block_major and (
    not page_contiguous
    and ((packed_storage and is_mla_region) or not self._is_csa_linear)
):
```

The gate is needed so a HiSparse decoder can land host-resident and device-only layers separately.
But `page_contiguous` is true for every GLM-5.3 layer, so a device-resident BLHNC cache registers one
region per layer. Every transfer then carries one descriptor per layer per block, and BLHNC
ends up costing more than LBHNC, the opposite of its purpose.

Registration on one GB200 decode rank, from the `prepared N descriptors into M strides` log line:

| layout | strides | descriptors |
|---|---:|---:|
| LBHNC, block 1024 | 62 | 2,488,080 |
| BLHNC, block 64, current main | 104 | 2,714,816 |
| BLHNC, block 64, whole row | 1 | 26,104 |

End to end, the whole-row run looked like this. GB200 runs: DEP8 prefill → 10× TP4 decode;
AgentX agentic traffic, 128 concurrent sessions, 1800 s per arm; 29,088 transfers.

| | LBHNC bs1024 | BLHNC bs64, whole row |
|---|---:|---:|
| NIXL xfer, mean | 85.23 ms | 22.30 ms |
| NIXL post, mean | 57.88 ms | 6.96 ms |
| TTFT p50 | 848 ms | 730 ms |

With fp8 KV on GB200 (DEP8 prefill → 1×TP8 decode, 32 sessions), current main's BLHNC took
2.0–3.6 s per transfer. Restoring the pre-#53781 gate brought that to 78 ms, against 146 ms for
LBHNC.

### 2. A naive re-enable misregisters a head-sharded draft
Under BLHNC, every KV cache group starts at byte 0 of the shared block row, so the first draft page
has the same base address as the first target page. Regions are deduplicated by base address.
So if the draft also takes the whole-row branch, it folds into the target's single replicated
region. Then #58471's per-rank head slice never runs, and each TP4 rank receives the TP1 prefill's
8-head draft pages unsliced. We shipped exactly that by narrowing the gate to
`(not page_contiguous or not self.use_host_buffer)`.

The same aliasing folds draft layer 0 into a target region even without whole-row: 104 strides
for 105 layers. That is #57661, fixed by #57662's `(base_addr, block_len)` key.

## Proposal (PR to follow, stacked on #58471 and #57662)
- Opt-in `kv_connector_extra_config.whole_row_regions` (default false).
- Replicated (MLA) layers of a block-major row register as one whole-row region.
- Head-sharded layers (a GQA draft under an MLA target) keep per-layer SPLIT regions, so each rank
  reads its own head slice.
- The flag is rejected with `kv_buffer_device=cpu` and with HiSparse host-resident groups, so
  #53781's case is untouched.
- With `--disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager`, BLHNC packs the head-sharded draft pages inside the
  target's block row. Their size depends on TP, so a whole-row region would differ between a TP1
  prefill and a TP4 decode (2,721,312 vs 2,131,360 bytes; the handshake asserts). The flag must reject
  that layout at registration with a clear error.

Open question for maintainers: should this be opt-in, or automatic whenever no group is
host-resident?

## Not this issue: DFlash2 acceptance under BLHNC
BLHNC deployments with a DFlash2 draft also lose about 5.5 points of draft acceptance. That loss is
tracked in #60560. It comes from the hybrid KV cache manager turning the sliding-window draft into a
real SWA group, not from NIXL registration: the corrected registration proposed here (B300, 34.18%)
loses as much as the misregistration described above (GB200, 34.8%).

## Before submitting a new issue...

items.title: [CAKE] Training Kernel Progress Tracker (Forward & Backward)
items.author: yyihuang
items.body_excerpt:
Training kernels deserve the whole CAKE, not just a forward slice. This issue tracks CAKE-generated kernels for end-to-end training workloads, with forward and backward paths baked together.

Have a training hotspot you want us to bake? Leave a comment or create a sub-issue with the operator, shapes, dtype, layout, target GPU, and baseline. We will put it in the oven! 🍰🔥

## Pull requests

### Linear attention

#### Recurrent KDA backward

- #5028 — fix the C16 forward triangular-matrix orientation in the recurrent KDA training implementation.

- #4636
- #4726 

#### Chunked KDA training backward

- #5376 — deterministic chunked training backward (chunk 64, K = V = 128, in-kernel Q/K L2 norm, lower-bound safe gate, sigmoid beta, `dt_bias`) for SM100a and SM103a: bit-identical repeated backward, 1.2–3.6x vs the flash-linear-attention v0.5.2 Triton backward on the Kimi K3 production rows

### Activation / quantization

#### Fused SwiGLU + MXFP8 quantization

- #4638 — fused forward and backward rowwise/colwise MXFP8 quantization for SM100a and SM103a

### Attention

#### Sparse MLA DSA with autograd (native 64 query heads: fwd, dQ, dKV)

- #5704
- #5737
- #6007
- #5865
- #6019

#### DSA indexer scoring + deterministic exact top-k (training)

- #5972
- #6056
- #6230

### LM-head and loss

#### Chunked LM-head + fused cross-entropy / policy loss with memory-bounded backward

- #5752
- #5897

### Normalization

#### Fused BF16 RMSNorm training (forward + backward)

- #5741

## Feature requests

### GLM-5.2 training on Rubin

- #5675 — native 64-head sparse MLA forward and backward: up to 2,048 segment-local keys per query, packed varlen with separate `cu_seqlens_q`/`cu_seqlens_k`, strided Q/KV views, and in-kernel scatter-add into packed FP32 dKV
- #5676 — DSA indexer scoring and top-k (H = 32, D = 128, K = 2048) with deterministic tie, ordering, signed-zero, and padding semantics
- #5677 — dense projection GEMMs (forward, dgrad, wgrad) on training operand layouts, including an FP32 router projection; validated cuBLASLt coverage is acceptable
- #5678 — MoE grouped GEMM forward, dgrad, and wgrad for ragged/empty groups, with deterministic FP32 wgrad; optional SwiGLU and routing-scale fusions
- #5679 — fused BF16 RMSNorm forward and backward (dx + dw), with FP32 statistics and no full `[T,H]` FP32 temporaries
- #5680 — chunked LM-head with cross-entropy and policy loss (V = 154,880), keeping logits/dlogits memory bounded by the token chunk
- #5997

items.title: Feature Request: Implement missing ops from backends
items.author: am17an
items.body_excerpt:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

The list of supported operation in ggml per backend is maintained at https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/docs/ops.md

How to contribute to make the list more complete:

1. Pick an operation which is not implemented in a backend (pick ones marked with ❌), pick only one per PR
2. Implement the operation
3. Test your implementation with `test-backend-ops -o <op>`
4. If it passes test for the op, create a PR.
5. Mention performance tests in the PR if they exist (via `test-backend-ops perf -o <op>`)

Notes:
1. The ops suffixed with _BACK are related to training which is WIP and does not require immediate attention
2. Do not link this issue in your PR, which will lead to closing this issue when your PR is merged. Instead, just mention it. Example PRs will be linked below
3. This list can be temporarily out of sync, you can check support by first running `test-backend-ops -o <op>` on master to confirm 
4. Please do not ask to be assigned a particular task, make the PR first if you think it will be useful


### Motivation

Feature parity between backends is always desirable and it's easy to test the implementation, making it an ideal good first issue.

### Possible Implementation

_No response_

comments.body:
> I would like to contribute to this effort. May I ask whether it is okay to work on operators marked as [🟡 Partially supported] in the ops.md table?

Yes that would also work. The reason it's preferable to work on completely unsupported ops is because sometimes it's not possible to add full support to an op on a backend (e.g. some quantisation schemes in CUDA) and it might not be clear as a newcomer why that's the case. But if you make an operation support more complete, that would always be welcome!

items.title: Misc. bug: server: flush metrics more frequently
items.author: hugendudel
items.body_excerpt:
### Name and Version

version: 0.6.0-dev (build 11429, commit d812350493)
built with GNU 16.2.1 for Linux x86_64


### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
llama-server --host 0.0.0.0 --port 11434 --metrics --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 -m /mnt/models/Qwen3-Coder-Next-Q4_K_M.gguf --temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 40 --min-p 0.01 --repeat-penalty 1.0 -c 262144
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

# server: flush metrics more frequently

## Overview

Currently, Prometheus metrics are only updated when `decode()` produces output (`has_output == true`). This causes metrics to be stale or incomplete in several scenarios:
- When tokens are cached and no output is produced
- When only embeddings are requested (no generation)
- When metrics tasks are queued behind other tasks

The metrics are updated in real-time in `update_slots()`, but when querying `/metrics`, the task goes through the queue. Pending metrics weren't being flushed before copying, resulting in delayed or incomplete metrics.

## Changes

- Always flush prompt metrics even when decode doesn't produce output
- Flush pending metrics before metrics task copies them for `/metrics` endpoint

This ensures Prometheus metrics are more up-to-date and reliable, matching the frequency of slot-level timing printouts.

## Additional information

### Before
- Metrics only updated when `has_output == true`
- `/metrics` endpoint could return stale data
- Prompt timing metrics missing for cached/embedding-only requests

### After
- Metrics flushed on every batch decode
- `/metrics` returns current state with pending metrics flushed
- Consistent metrics regardless of decode output type

items.title: Misc. bug: server: RAM prompt cache restores KV computed under a different LoRA configuration
items.author: wu69137-alt
items.body_excerpt:
### Name and Version

$ ./llama-server --version
version: 0.5.0-dev (build 1, commit 11fe021)
built with GNU 9.4.0 for Linux x86_64

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
llama-server -m base.gguf --lora A.gguf --lora-init-without-apply -np 1 -c 4096 --host 127.0.0.1
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

### What happened
When the RAM prompt cache is enabled (the default), a restored KV entry does not
record or check the LoRA setting it was computed with. So even though LoRA is
explicitly specified for each request, we can still get KV that was computed
under another LoRA setting.

### How to reproduce
llama-server -m <base>.gguf --lora <A>.gguf --lora-init-without-apply -np 1 -c 4096

Send 3 requests:
1. P with `"lora":[{"id":0,"scale":0}]`
2. Q with `"lora":[{"id":0,"scale":1}]`
3. P with `"lora":[{"id":0,"scale":1}]`

Why Q? Q takes the only slot, so P is moved into the RAM prompt cache.

On request 3, we found that the KV for P is restored from the cache entry written
by request 1 (`cache_n` ≈ 874, `prompt_n` = 1). This means a request under scale 1
is decoded on KV computed under scale 0.

### Results
We ran the 3 steps above with 20 different prompts. For all 20 prompts, the
step 3 output differs from the golden label (20/20), which is the output of
running P alone under scale 1 with `cache_prompt: false`. Three of them are
exactly the same as the output under scale 0.

We also ran it again with `--cache-ram 0`. The results match the golden label
(0/20 differ).

Changing step 1 to scale 1 also gives the expected result (0/20 differ), even
though the cache is still reused.

### Expected
We expect that there should be a LoRA checking mechanism when fetching the KV
from the RAM prompt cache.

### Related
It's similar to #26207, but in this case the path goes through the RAM prompt
cache, which seems different.

items.title: [Store] Proposal: S3-compatible ObjectStorageAdapter for the distributed storage backend
items.author: pingqiu
items.body_excerpt:
### Proposal: an S3-compatible `ObjectStorageAdapter` for the distributed storage backend

`docs/source/design/store/oss-backend.md` notes that key-based storage services such as OSS and S3 plug in through service-specific adapters, and that S3 needs a compatible adapter rather than a different endpoint. We would like to contribute that adapter, so Mooncake Store can offload to any S3-compatible store: AWS S3, SeaweedFS, MinIO, Ceph RGW and others.

**Proposed shape**

- A new `"s3"` value for `fs_adapter_type`, next to `"oss"` in `storage_backend.cpp`, behind the same libcurl + OpenSSL build condition.
- Reading `oss_adapter.cpp`, almost everything is protocol-neutral: URI encoding, canonical query, LIST XML parsing, the curl multi batch engine, iovec uploads and range reads. The OSS-specific parts are `BuildUrl`, `BuildAuthorization` and the `x-oss-*` header names in `PrepareRequest`. We would factor the shared part into a common base and add an S3 subclass with AWS Signature V4 (`AWS4-HMAC-SHA256`, `x-amz-*` headers), path-style addressing and a custom endpoint. The OSS adapter's behaviour would not change.
- Configuration with the same shape as the OSS adapter: endpoint, bucket, region, access key, secret, session token, path style, max connections and buffer sizes, read from `MOONCAKE_S3_*` environment variables (or whatever prefix you prefer).

**Tests**

- S3 versions of `oss_adapter_test.cpp` and `oss_adapter_config_test.cpp`, and a live test helper like `oss_live_test_helpers.h`.
- Live runs against SeaweedFS and MinIO, plus a store-level run that offloads through `kDistributed` + `s3` and reads everything back.

**Questions before we start**

1. Is a shared base with the OSS adapter acceptable, or would you prefer a standalone S3 adapter, or one built on the AWS SDK already linked for HA snapshots (`common/s3_helper.h`)?
2. Any preference for the environment variable prefix or the build flag name?

Happy to adjust the plan to whatever fits the project best.

items.title: [Bug]: Ascend NPU build - loading mooncake.store aborts the process at exit (heap corruption -> SIGABRT)
items.author: brandneway
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

On the Ascend NPU build, merely loading the Python extension `mooncake.store` (or `mooncake.engine`) makes **any process abort during interpreter shutdown**, even though nothing else is done with Mooncake. glibc reports a corrupted heap block and raises SIGABRT, so the process exits with a non-zero status.

This is not about *using* Mooncake: the failure fires in processes that only import it and then exit normally.

### Environment

- Package: `mooncake-transfer-engine-npu` **0.3.11.post1** (the wheel reports itself as "Python binding of a Mooncake library using pybind11 (Ascend NPU version)")
- Hardware: Atlas 800I A3 server, 8x Ascend910 (16 dies)
- CANN: **9.1.0** (`/usr/local/Ascend/cann-9.1.0`)
- OS / libc: aarch64 Linux (glibc), Python 3.12

### Reproduction

```bash
$ python3 -c "import mooncake.store"
corrupted size vs. prev_size
Aborted (core dumped)          # rc=134, 5/5 runs
```

`mooncake.engine` behaves identically. Two refinements that narrow it down:

```bash
# 1. No Mooncake Python code has to run -- dlopen of the extension alone is enough
$ python3 -c "import ctypes; ctypes.CDLL('<site-packages>/mooncake/store.so')"
corrupted size vs. prev_size
Aborted (core dumped)          # rc=134, 5/5 runs

# 2. It only happens on the normal-exit path
$ python3 -c "import mooncake.store, os; os._exit(0)"     # rc=0  (skips shutdown)
$ python3 -c "import mooncake"                            # rc=0  (package __init__ is empty)
```

### Backtrace

```
corrupted size vs. prev_size
Program received signal SIGABRT
#0  __pthread_kill_implementation
#1  __pthread_kill_internal
#2  __GI_raise
#3  __GI_abort
#4  __libc_message
#5  malloc_printerr  <-- "corrupted size vs. prev_size"
#6  unlink_chunk          (malloc.c:1629)
#7  malloc_consolidate    (malloc.c:4779)
#8  _int_free             (malloc.c:4674)
#9  __GI___libc_free
#10 ?? () from /usr/local/Ascend/cann-9.1.0/lib64/libascend_trace.so
#11 ?? () from /usr/local/Ascend/cann-9.1.0/lib64/libascend_trace.so
#12 ?? () from /usr/local/Ascend/cann-9.1.0/lib64/libascend_trace.so
#13 _dl_fini              (elf/dl-fini.c:142)
#14 __run_exit_handlers
#15 __GI_exit
#16 __libc_start_call_main
```

`free` is called from a CANN finalizer in `libascend_trace.so` during `_dl_fini`; the block it is releasing was already corrupt by then.

### What we ruled out

| Hypothesis | Experiment | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Python object heap corruption | `PYTHONMALLOC=debug` | nothing reported — this is the C `malloc` heap |
| Mooncake's Python code | `ctypes.CDLL(store.so)` with no Python code running | still aborts |
| A single offending shared object | `ctypes.CDLL()` on `libcann_hixl.so`, `libllm_datadist.so`, `libascend_trace.so` individually | all exit 0 |
| A generic "load a lot of CANN libs" issue | `import torch_npu` (also maps `libascend_trace.so`) | exits 0 |
| The exit path itself | `os._exit(0)` | exits 0 — confirms shutdown-only |

`ldd store.so` shows it links ~34 CANN libraries, among them `libcann_hixl.so`, `libllm_datadist.so`, `ascend_transport.so` (the latter ships inside the mooncake package itself).

### What we could not determine

We did **not** identify which code writes the corrupted bytes. Binary-searching the CANN library set produced **non-monotonic** results — a 10-library subset loads cleanly while dropping one of several members makes it abort again — which is the signature of heap-layout-sensitive corruption rather than a deterministic API misuse. `GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.malloc.check=3` also fails to catch it any earlier. The `free` on the stack is a victim, not the culprit.

### Impact

Any short-lived process that imports `mooncake.store` and then exits normally is reported as failed by its parent, because the exit status is non-zero even though the work completed. Concretely, this breaks vLLM-Omni: the subprocess vLLM forks to inspect model architectures imports the whole vllm-omni package, so it dies on the way out and the parent refuses to start the deployment:

```
RuntimeError: Model architectures ['MiniMaxH3Encoder'] failed to be inspected
```

This makes every Ascend deployment containing an LLM stage fail to start. Reported upstream in vllm-project/vllm-omni#8624, which works around it by no longer importing the optional connectors eagerly — but that only removes the *accidental* exposure; a deployment that genuinely selects a Mooncake connector still hits this abort.

We would appreciate any pointers on whether this is a known issue with the Ascend build, whether it is fixed in a newer wheel, or which component to follow up with.

items.title: `[Inductor][CUDA] FTZ on subnormal inputs causes O(1) errors in ceil(float32) and atan2(bfloat16)`
items.author: tinywisdom
items.body_excerpt:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

On CUDA, Inductor's default flush-to-zero (FTZ) flushes subnormal **inputs** to (signed) zero before the operation, which turns mathematically correct **normal-scale** outputs into wrong ones. Unlike the "a subnormal output is flushed" cases, here the expected outputs (`1`, `π/4`) are normal-scale and exactly representable, so this is an O(1) correctness error, not a lost tiny mantissa.

```python
import torch

# 1) ceil(float32 subnormal): eager [1,1], inductor [0,0]
x = torch.tensor([1e-45, 2e-45], device='cuda', dtype=torch.float32)   # positive fp32 subnormals
print(torch.ceil(x))                                        # tensor([1., 1.], device='cuda:0')
print(torch.compile(torch.ceil)(x))                         # tensor([0., 0.], device='cuda:0')   # FTZ: ceil(0)=0

# 2) atan2(bfloat16 subnormal): eager -pi/4, inductor -0.0 (amplified by a following cos)
x = torch.tensor(1e-38, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device='cuda')          # bf16 subnormal
y = torch.tensor(1e-38, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device='cuda')
f = lambda x, y: torch.cos(torch.atan2(torch.neg(x), y))
print(f(x, y))                                              # tensor(0.7070, ...)  (cos(-pi/4))
print(torch.compile(f)(x, y))                               # tensor(1.,     ...)  (atan2 -> -0.0, cos(0)=1)
```

**Mechanism confirmed by a single control:** setting
`torch._inductor.config.eager_numerics.disable_ftz = True` restores both to the correct values (`ceil -> [1,1]`, `atan2 -> -pi/4`, `cos-chain -> 0.707`), confirming a single kernel-level FTZ mechanism.

**Expected:** compiled `ceil`/`atan2` match eager on subnormal inputs (`[1,1]` and `-pi/4`).

### Versions

```
PyTorch version: 2.15.0a0+git1a080e5
Is debug build: True
CUDA used to build PyTorch: 12.6
ROCM used to build PyTorch: N/A

OS: Ubuntu 22.04.4 LTS (x86_64)

items.body_excerpt:
HybridLinear/Mamba models such as Nemotron-H have a pre-existing HiCache correctness issue with pipeline parallelism (`PP > 1`). On non-first stages, cache-transfer completion and consumers use different layer indices, so forward may read cached state before host-to-device restoration finishes.

PR #37870 fixes sparse layer-ID coverage for `PP=1`. PP support needs a separate correctness review and end-to-end validation; this issue tracks that follow-up.

The top-level CMakeLists.txt in Triton links the LLVM codegen libraries for the host CPU architecture (e.g., LLVMX86CodeGen or LLVMAArch64CodeGen).

My understanding is that Triton only needs the GPU backends, such as AMDGPU and NVPTX, to generate GPU code. If that's correct, could you explain why the host CPU codegen libraries are also required? Specifically, which parts of Triton or LLVM depend on them, and where are they used?

If my understanding is incorrect, I'd appreciate it if you could clarify.

CMake code used to link the codegen library:
```Cmake
  if(CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR MATCHES "aarch64" OR # Linux arm64
     CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR MATCHES "arm64" OR # macOS arm64
     CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES MATCHES "arm64")  # also macOS arm64
      list(APPEND TRITON_LIBRARIES
          LLVMAArch64CodeGen
          LLVMAArch64AsmParser
      )
  elseif(CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR MATCHES "x86_64" OR CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR MATCHES "AMD64")
      list(APPEND TRITON_LIBRARIES
          LLVMX86CodeGen
          LLVMX86AsmParser
      )
  elseif(CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR MATCHES "ppc64le")
      list(APPEND TRITON_LIBRARIES
        LLVMPowerPCAsmParser
        LLVMPowerPCCodeGen
      )
  else()
    message(FATAL_ERROR "LLVM codegen/ASM parser libs: This HW architecture (${CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR}) is not configured in cmake lib dependencies.")
  endif()
```

items.title: `tl.argmin`/`tl.argmax` return a NaN lane despite finite extrema
items.author: merlinsun
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

With one NaN and finite extrema in the same reduction, the compiled kernel returned the NaN lane as both the minimum and maximum index, while returning the finite minimum and maximum values. For example, with `x = [-13.0, -1.0, 17.0, NaN]`, the probe observed `min_value=-13`, `max_value=17`, `min_index=3`, and `max_index=3`; the finite-value indices are `0` and `2`.

Minimal kernel:

```python
import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl

@triton.jit
def kernel(x_ptr, min_idx_ptr, max_idx_ptr):
    x = tl.load(x_ptr + tl.arange(0, 4))
    tl.store(min_idx_ptr, tl.argmin(x, axis=0))
    tl.store(max_idx_ptr, tl.argmax(x, axis=0))

x = torch.tensor([-13.0, -1.0, 17.0, float("nan")],
                 device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
min_idx = torch.empty((), device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
max_idx = torch.empty_like(min_idx)
kernel[(1,)](x, min_idx, max_idx)
torch.cuda.synchronize()
print(min_idx, max_idx)  # probe observed 3, 3; finite extrema are at 0, 2
```

### Environment details

Triton https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/commit/4fd7cc5cfd0a84acfeb5dadb1578dffa409903fc on A800

items.title: [Rprop] Negative step_sizes are accepted and can reverse the parameter update direction
items.author: Mohit-25-tech
items.body_excerpt:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

`torch.optim.Rprop` accepts negative values for `step_sizes`.

For example, `step_sizes=(-2.0, -1.0)` is accepted by the constructor. On the first optimization step, the stored step size becomes `-1.0`. With a positive gradient, this reverses the expected update direction and moves the parameter upward instead of downward.

I reproduced this with both `foreach=False` and `foreach=True`.

### Minimal reproduction

```python
import torch

print("PyTorch:", torch.__version__)

for foreach in (False, True):
    p = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.tensor([1.0]))

    opt = torch.optim.Rprop(
        [p],
        lr=0.01,
        step_sizes=(-2.0, -1.0),
        foreach=foreach,
    )

    p.grad = torch.tensor([1.0])
    opt.step()

    print(
        f"foreach={foreach}, "
        f"parameter={p.item()}, "
        f"step_size={opt.state[p]['step_size'].item()}"
    )
```

On `torch 2.16.0.dev20261007+cpu`, both paths produced:

```text
parameter=2.0
step_size=-1.0
```

The parameter starts at `1.0` with gradient `+1.0`, but moves to `2.0` because the negative step size reverses the update direction.

For comparison, with the normal `step_sizes=(1e-6, 50.0)`, the parameter moves from `1.0` to approximately `0.99`.

### Expected behavior

I would expect Rprop to reject negative step-size bounds rather than allowing its internal step magnitude to become negative.

I noticed that the existing tests intentionally allow a minimum step size of `0`, so a possible validation rule appears to be:

```python
0 <= step_sizes[0] <= step_sizes[1]
```

This would preserve `(0, 50)` while rejecting negative and reversed bounds.

### Proposed fix / maintainer guidance

The minimal solution I have in mind is to validate `step_sizes` in the `Rprop` constructor using the rule above.

I have also worked through regression/error-validation cases for:

- `(-2.0, -1.0)` — negative bounds
- `(-1.0, 50.0)` — negative minimum
- `(2.0, 1.0)` — reversed bounds

Could a maintainer please confirm whether `0 <= step_sizes[0] <= step_sizes[1]` is the intended constraint?

If this issue is considered actionable, I am ready to submit a focused PR with the validation change and regression coverage.

### AI assistance disclosure

I used OpenAI Codex to assist with inspecting the Rprop implementation, identifying the missing validation, and exploring the relevant test coverage.

I manually reviewed the proposed logic and independently reproduced the behavior in Kaggle for both `foreach=False` and `foreach=True`.

I also searched for an existing issue or PR covering negative or reversed Rprop `step_sizes` but did not find an equivalent report. Please let me know if I missed an existing discussion.

items.title: SM120: FlashInfer autotune exceeds NCCL pair timeout — all workers crash after ~50 min with "Application timeout caused pair closure"
items.author: xzwgit
items.body_excerpt:
## Environment

- GPU: 8× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120, cc 12.0)
- Driver / CUDA: 595.71.05 / CUDA 13.2.2
- FlashInfer: 0.7.1 (source build from main, with CUTLASS/CCCL headers linked per #5873)
- vLLM: nightly dev511, `--kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"flashinfer_cutlass"}'`

## Problem

The first-boot FlashInfer autotune (`mxfp8_gemm`, 21 profiles) runs for >50 minutes on SM120. During this time, the 8 TP workers' NCCL pairs are idle and exceed the timeout threshold. When the autotune finishes and the warmup dummy run starts calling `flashinfer_cutlass_fused_moe`, the NCCL communication is already dead:

```
RuntimeError: Application timeout caused pair closure
```

All 8 workers crash simultaneously. The AutoTuner itself completes successfully (21/21 profiles at ~230 profile/s) — the crash happens in the subsequent warmup phase.

## Timeline

| Phase | Duration | Status |
|---|---|---|
| FlashInfer JIT compilation | ~15 min | ✅ |
| AutoTuner (mxfp8_gemm, 21 profiles) | ~27 min | ✅ completes |
| Warmup dummy run | — | ❌ NCCL already dead |

## Workaround

`--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune` (same flag used in the RTX PRO 6000 recipes for other models). Service starts in ~1 minute, correctness verified (17×19=323), FlashInfer CUTLASS kernels work without tuning.

However, this means SM120 users get untuned kernels. On B300 (SM100), autotuned FlashInfer is 30~54% faster than DeepGEMM; without autotune on SM120, FlashInfer is only +8~12% faster at c8+ and -5~11% slower at c1~c4.

## Suggested fix

One of:
1. Increase NCCL timeout during autotune (or set NCCL_KEEP_ALIVE or similar)
2. Make autotune communicate periodically with NCCL pairs to keep them alive
3. Run autotune in a separate process before starting the engine (pre-tune CLI tool)
4. Warn users about this timeout and auto-set `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune` on SM120 when first boot is detected

This issue is distinct from #5873 (missing headers) — both must be fixed for a smooth SM120 first-boot experience.

items.title: [SM120 sparse MLA] smem static_asserts check the dynamic size only; the per-block limit is static + dynamic
items.author: Col-5555
items.body_excerpt:
Low priority, and nothing fails today: this is a robustness note from a shared-memory audit we did for GLM-5.3 on GB10 (sm_121).

**What the asserts check.** In `kernels/fp8_prefill/smem_layout.cuh` on main (`common/smem_layout.cuh` in v0.7.0), the SG, MG and swapAB layouts each have `static_assert(TOTAL <= 101376, "... smem exceeds 99KB per-block limit")`, where `TOTAL` is the dynamic shared memory the launcher requests. The per-block limit applies to static and dynamic shared memory together. On GB10 the opt-in maximum is 101,376 B (`sharedMemPerBlockOptin`), and CUDA documents that `cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize` plus the kernel's `sharedSizeBytes` cannot exceed it. Every GLM-5.3 sparse-MLA kernel in our build has 1,024 B of static shared memory (`cuobjdump -res-usage`). So a layout with a dynamic `TOTAL` between 100,353 and 101,376 B would pass the assert and then fail at `cudaFuncSetAttribute` or launch time. The decode path has no compile-time check; its budget is a comment ("Grand total ≈ 98 KB (under 99 KB sm120a carveout)"), which does count the static buffer.

**Margins today.** For GLM-5.3 with FP8, static + dynamic, using our transcription of the v0.7.0 layout formulas: decode 81,200 B, prefill SG 83,344, MG 92,944, swapAB 94,240. That leaves at least 7,136 B of headroom, so nothing is close for this model. The tightest budget we saw is the DSv3.2 decode comment's ≈ 98 KB.

**Suggestion.** Either reserve a static budget in the asserts (for example `TOTAL + kStaticSmemBudget <= 101376`), or check at launch with `cudaFuncGetAttributes` (`sharedSizeBytes` + requested dynamic ≤ `sharedMemPerBlockOptin`) and raise an error that names the kernel and both sizes, rather than a generic CUDA error. If our nodes are free at the time, we're happy to test a change on GB10.

_Drafted with Claude Code. Static sizes were measured with `cuobjdump` on our build; dynamic sizes are transcribed from the layout code at v0.7.0 (`4d75a33f`)._

items.title: [Bug] FlashInfer autotune cache is discarded every boot under MoE expert parallelism (EP>1): per-rank shapes never agree, so the fused-MoE tactic is re-drawn each start
items.author: ntxf31415
items.body_excerpt:
### Summary

`_drop_diverged_autotune_cache()` discards the whole FlashInfer autotune cache — on every boot — whenever the per-rank MoE GEMM shapes differ, which is the normal case with **expert parallelism (EP > 1)**. The cache is then re-tuned from scratch each start, so the fused-MoE tactic is re-drawn every boot. Since the tactic selection is timing-based, end-to-end throughput varies across boots with identical config.

### Environment

- 4× GB10 (DGX Spark), SGLang TP4 / EP2, switchless RoCE ring
- MoE runner backend `flashinfer_mxfp4` (MXFP4 experts), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
- `--chunked-prefill-size 4096`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.90`
- FlashInfer 0.6.18, CUDA 13.0, cuDNN 92000

### Root cause

`python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/flashinfer_autotune.py`:

```python
def _autotune_cache_digest(cache_path, env):
    ...
    payload = {"file": configs, "env": env}
    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()

def _drop_diverged_autotune_cache(cache_path, group, env) -> None:
    digests = [""] * torch.distributed.get_world_size(group)
    torch.distributed.all_gather_object(digests, _autotune_cache_digest(cache_path, env), group=group)
    if len(set(digests)) == 1:
        return
    ...
    cache_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)          # <-- deletes the cache
```

Each rank digests **its own** `rank_tp{N}_pp0_dp0.json` and all four are compared. Under EP sharding each rank owns a different slice of the routed experts, so **the MoE GEMM problem shapes themselves differ per rank** and the files can never be equal. Measured on our four ranks (same boot, same config, caches cleared so all four start from empty):

| rank | distinct shapes in its cache | example expert shape present |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 24 | `(192, 2304, 320)` |
| 1 | 24 | `(64, 2304, 320)` |
| 2 | 24 | `(64, 2304, 320)` / `(192, …)` |
| 3 | 24 | `(16, 5120)`, `(4, 5120)` |

**The intersection of the four shape sets is empty.** So `len(set(digests)) == 1` is never true, the cache is `unlink`ed on every start, and every start re-profiles `trtllm::fused_moe::gemm1` / `gemm2` for all shapes.

Startup log, one boot:

```
Running FlashInfer autotune with cache: /root/.cache/sglang/flashinfer/autotune/0.6.18/sm121/<key>/rank_tp3_pp0_dp0.json
[AutoTuner]: Tuning trtllm::fused_moe::gemm1:   0%|          | 0/8 ...
```

Tuning count is **26–27 profiles per boot** regardless of whether a complete cache file is already present at that path. The shipped image cache contains only `sparse_mla_sm120_decode_dsv4` entries, so the fused-MoE shapes always miss anyway.

Note the digest also includes the environment, so even equal tactics would not be enough — but here the file contents themselves cannot match.

### Impact

The fused-MoE tactic is re-drawn on every start, and it matters a lot. Two consecutive boots of the same configuration, measured with a cold single-stream prefill probe at 8K tokens:

| boot | prefill t/s (8K) |
|---|---|
| A | 3169 |
| B | 2431 |

**−23 % at 8K**, while 100K was essentially unchanged (3266 vs 3164) — i.e. the draw is shape-range dependent, and a bad draw is stable for the whole life of that process. We also saw a full 1.5× swing on longer inputs between boots.

### Workaround we run

We mount a site-patched copy of this file that keeps the digest check and the log line but drops the `unlink`:

```python
    log_info_on_rank0(logger, "[site patch] keeping per-rank autotune caches")
```

With the per-rank caches kept, subsequent boots report **0 tuning profiles** (cache genuinely read and used) and throughput is stable.

⚠️ Caveat we found the hard way: this is only safe if every rank's own cache is **complete**. If some ranks hit and others miss, the missing ranks enter the timing-reduction collective while the others don't — we reproduced that as an NCCL collective timeout at startup with the process hanging, so a partial cache is worse than none.

### Possible fix directions

1. Compare like-for-like per rank (i.e. make the guard per-rank rather than requiring cross-rank equality), given that under EP the shape sets legitimately differ.
2. Or key the digest only on the *tactics for the shapes this rank actually uses*, rather than on the whole file.
3. Or make the reduction group follow the ranks that actually share a shape set.

If the divergence check is load-bearing for a reason we have not understood, it may be worth at least not deleting — logging and continuing — so a partially-cached fleet degrades to slow rather than to a hang.

items.title: Idle-wake hang at _low_ratio_index_topk_dense when --sleep-on-idle is enabled (post-#40111 prefill host-sync path)
items.author: wzhizhi
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

Engine hangs (wakes into a dead prefill) when `--sleep-on-idle` is enabled on a build that includes the prefill-indexer host-sync changes from #40111 (cherry-picked onto our fork base `gefa7be209`).

After ~10-20 minutes of idle (engine asleep), any request that wakes the scheduler stalls forever inside the low-ratio dense indexer path. The API stops responding (`/health` returns nothing, container stays `Up` but unhealthy). No traceback, no OOM, no kernel events. One occurrence ended in exit code 255 instead.

### Reproduction

- 3x DGX Spark (GB10, SM121, UMA), TP=3, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSPARK speculative decoding
- Base: sglang fork at `gefa7be209` (~09-20) + #40111 + #40658 cherry-picked cleanly
- `--sleep-on-idle` in EXTRA_SGLANG_ARGS; idle for 10-20 min; then send any request (even a monitoring probe)
- py-spy dump (two samples, identical):

```
_low_ratio_index_topk_dense (indexer_chunked_v3.py:181)
_low_ratio_index_topk_extend (deepseek_v4_backend.py:3216)
_low_ratio_index_topk (deepseek_v4_backend.py:3192)
forward_low_ratio_sources (deepseek_v4_backend.py:2852)
...
execute (runner/eager_runner.py:228)
forward (prefill_empty_cache.py:37)
forward_batch_generation (tp_worker.py:674)
```

The wake path runs `prefill_empty_cache` (an empty-cache prefill) and never returns from `_low_ratio_index_topk_dense`.

### Environment

- sglang fork base `gefa7be209` + #40111/#40658
- 3x NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10), driver 615.71.09, NCCL 2.32.3
- Happens on every idle->wake cycle after the patch; base without the patch survives idle nights on the same hardware.

### Workaround

Removing `--sleep-on-idle` eliminates the hang entirely (engine stays resident through idle). Posting in case the host-sync removal in the prefill slot path has a missed synchronization point on the wake-from-sleep re-capture path — worth a look if others see idle-wake hangs on recent builds.

items.title: Same-type fp8 arithmetic passes the frontend and fails in LLVM lowering
items.author: LiRunGuo
items.body_excerpt:
`computation_type_impl` returns the fp8 type itself for same-type fp8 operands (rule added in #4222 so `tl.where` works on fp8, and asserted in `test_fp8_div_mod_promotion`: `(x * y).dtype == tl.float8e5`). But no backend can lower fp8 arithmetic, so `+ - *`, unary `-`, comparisons, `x * 2`, and `tl.sum` on an fp8 tensor all fail late with a verifier error instead of a frontend diagnostic:

```python
@triton.jit
def kernel(X, Y):
    offs = tl.arange(0, 128)
    x = tl.load(X + offs)          # *fp8e4nv
    tl.store(Y + offs, x * 2)
```
```
error: 'llvm.fmul' op operand #0 must be floating point LLVM type ..., but got 'i8'
RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed
```

Same on sm90/sm100 and gfx942/gfx950. `tl.maximum`, `tl.abs`, `tl.where`, `/` (promoted to fp32) work. Before #4222 this was a frontend `TypeError` (#2640, where fp8 arithmetic was described as expected-unsupported).

Options: (a) raise a clear frontend error for arithmetic/comparison on same-type fp8 while keeping selection ops (`where`, `maximum`, ...) fp8, or (b) promote same-type fp8 to fp16 like mixed fp8 already does (dtype-visible change). Happy to send whichever is preferred.

items.title: tl.dot_scaled in a loop: TritonGPUOptimizeAccumulatorInit PassManager::run failed on a non-carried accumulator
items.author: dkarpman
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

`TritonGPUOptimizeAccumulatorInit` aborts (`PassManager::run failed`) on a loop body whose `tl.dot_scaled` result is **not carried by a reassigned accumulator variable** — i.e. a fresh result tensor is bound each iteration. Every *reassigned-carried* accumulator form (the `acc=` argument, `acc += ...`, or a reset-per-iteration) compiles at all shapes tested.

This blocks `tl.dot_scaled` (mxfp4) kernels authored as a plain loop (the natural DeepGEMM-style persistent/tiled form).

### Reproducer (minimal, standalone)

```python
import torch, triton, triton.language as tl

@triton.jit
def _loop_dot_scaled(lhs, lhs_sf, rhs, rhs_sf, out, NBLK: tl.constexpr):
    rn = tl.arange(0, 128); rk2 = tl.arange(0, 64); rs = tl.arange(0, 4)
    for blk in tl.range(0, NBLK, num_stages=2):
        off = blk * 128
        a = tl.load(lhs + (off + rn)[:, None] * 64 + rk2[None, :]).to(tl.uint8)
        a_sf = tl.load(lhs_sf + (off + rn)[:, None] * 4 + rs[None, :])
        b = tl.load(rhs + rk2[:, None] * 64 * NBLK + (off + rn)[None, :]).to(tl.uint8)
        b_sf = tl.load(rhs_sf + (off + rn)[:, None] * 4 + rs[None, :])
        acc = tl.dot_scaled(a, a_sf, "e2m1", b, b_sf, "e2m1", out_dtype=tl.float32)
        tl.store(out + (off + rn)[:, None] * 128 + rn[None, :], acc)
```

Launch with NBLK=8 on an sm100 device against zero-initialized uint8 operands shaped `(NBLK*128, 64)` / `(NBLK*128, 4)` (LHS), `(64, NBLK*128)` / `(NBLK*128, 4)` (RHS), fp32 out `(NBLK*128, 128)`.

Expected: compiles and runs. Actual:

```
error: Failures have been detected while processing an MLIR pass pipeline
note: Pipeline failed while executing [`TritonGPUOptimizeAccumulatorInit` on 'builtin.module' operation]
RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed
```

### What compiles vs crashes (measured)

| form | carrier | result |
|---|---|---|
| fresh per-iter `acc = tl.dot_scaled(...)`, loop-invariant operands | none | CRASH |
| fresh per-iter `acc = ...`, fresh operand loads per iter | none | CRASH |
| fresh per-iter `acc = ...`, MMA-N = 64 | none | CRASH |
| loop-invariant `zacc` passed as `acc=zacc` (never reassigned) | `acc=` (invariant) | CRASH |
| `acc += tl.dot_scaled(...)` (reassigned) | `+=` | OK |
| `acc = tl.dot_scaled(..., acc=acc)` (reassigned) | `acc=` | OK |
| `acc = acc * 0.0; acc = tl.dot_scaled(..., acc=acc)` (reassigned) | `acc=` | OK |
| nested: outer tile loop, inner carried-acc `tl.range(num_stages=2)` | `acc=` (reassigned) | OK |
| `tl.static_range` full unroll with fresh per-iter acc | n/a | OK |

The trigger is the non-reassigned result: it is independent of the MMA shape and the pipeline depth (also crashes with `num_stages=1` and a plain Python `range`).

### Environment

- Triton: 3.8.0
- GPU: NVIDIA B200 (sm100), CUDA 13.3
- Relevant pass: `lib/Dialect/TritonGPU/Transforms/OptimizeAccumulatorInit.cpp`

items.title: [RFC] Review MC_USE_TENT=1 gaps for classic TE callers
items.author: staryxchen
items.body_excerpt:
## How this list was produced

Started as a static pass over:

- the C++ shim (`mooncake-transfer-engine/src/transfer_engine.cpp`, `use_tent_` branches)
- the Python wrapper (`mooncake-integration/transfer_engine/transfer_engine_py.cpp`)
- inference-engine call sites that use `mooncake.engine.TransferEngine`

Local runtime (2026-09-10, installed TENT wheel, 1P1D PD) then confirmed
some items and left others unverified. Status below is as of **2026-09-17**
(`origin/main` `c4d632888b`). Please still reproduce on your tree before
treating a remaining item as confirmed.

## Why the compatibility layer

We are wiring inference engines to TENT's **native** APIs, but that work is
not finished. Until it is, we use the classic TE compatibility layer
(`MC_USE_TENT=1`) to validate TENT **runtime** stability against existing
callers (PD disaggregation and others). This RFC tracks gaps in that layer.
It is not the native-API migration itself.

## Summary

`MC_USE_TENT=1` (and `MC_USE_TEV1=1`) is meant to run existing
`mooncake::TransferEngine` / `mooncake.engine.TransferEngine` code on the TENT
runtime. Register + sync submit/poll are wired up enough for PD KV transfer.

PD happy path **works** under `MC_USE_TENT=1` (local 1P1D Qwen3-4B
`/generate` 200). This RFC is not a claim that PD is broken today.

Most of the original P0/P1/P2 shim holes now have merged PRs. What is still
open is protocol pinning for `efa`/`ascend`, Python sync/poll semantics, and
`installTransport()` returning `nullptr` for classic C/Go/EFA callers.

If you find a **new** compatibility-layer issue, please report it on this
issue. We will add it to the work-item list.

## Non-goals

- Landing inference-engine (or Mooncake Store) native-API migration in this RFC
  (that work is separate and in progress, e.g. #4070).
- Teaching applications to `installTransport` under TENT. Making the shim
  honor the classic `Transport*` contract so existing callers do not treat a
  successful TENT init as failure **is** in scope (`P1-install-transport`).
- Changing TENT runtime scheduling / failover policy.

## Work items

Priority is "if the reading holds, impact is high" — not "already on fire".

| ID | Problem | Difficulty | PR | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P0-send_probe | Python `send_probe` SIGSEGV (`getMetadata()` is null) | M | #4081, follow-up #4115 | **done** |
| P0-stale-handle | Transfer failure may keep a dead peer's cached handle (`CheckSegmentStatus` was always OK) | M | #4109 | **partial** |
| P0-device-filter | `initialize(device=...)` still opened all HCAs | M | #4028 | **done** |
| P0-force-tcp | `MC_FORCE_TCP=1` / `protocol=tcp` may still select RDMA | M | #4027, follow-up #4113 | **done** |
| P0-efa-ascend | `protocol=efa\|ascend` may no-op or look successful without that transport | H | — | **open** |
| P1-sync-status | Python `transferSync` retry / `CANCELED` handling may not match TENT failover | S–M | — | **open** |
| P1-error-codes | Shim returned TENT `Status::Code` (non-negative); classic callers expect `ERR_*` | M | #4139 | **done** |
| P1-request-options | `priority` / `remote_accessible` were dropped at the shim | M | #4114 | **done** |
| P2-first-buffer | `getFirstBufferAddress` also called `getMetadata()` (same null deref as `send_probe`) | S | #4138 | **done** |
| P1-install-transport | TENT `installTransport()` returns `nullptr`; classic C/Go/EFA callers treat that as install failure | M | — | **open** |

### Residuals on landed items

These do not reopen the row, but they are not "the original hole is gone with no leftover":

- **P0-send_probe.** Python no longer dereferences `getMetadata()`. #4081 closed the segment after probing, which invalidated a handle already stored in Python `handle_map_`; #4115 stopped closing it. C++ `getMetadata()` is still `nullptr` under TENT — any remaining `getMetadata()->sendProbe` caller will still crash.
- **P0-stale-handle.** `CheckSegmentStatus` now probes via `probePeerAliveByID`. Python only calls it when **`submitTransfer` fails**. Peer death that shows up as `getTransferStatus` `FAILED` / `TIMEOUT` still leaves `handle_map_` intact. That leftover belongs with **P1-sync-status**. The unit test covers an never-opened handle, not a still-mapped handle whose RPC probe fails.
- **P0-force-tcp.** #4113 makes `forceTcp()` disable HP TCP so a config with both enabled does not fail init.
- **P1-error-codes.** Integer-returning APIs go through `tentToClassicError()`. `submitTransfer` still wraps TENT failures as `Status::Context(...)`. No in-tree test that failed on main and passed after (#4139 checklist).
- **P1-request-options.** Shim forwards `remote_accessible` → TENT perms and `TransferRequest::priority` on submit. Python `transferSync` does not set `priority` (default MEDIUM). No in-tree red/green test (#4114 checklist).

### Still open

- **P0-efa-ascend.** `init(..., protocol)` is now forwarded, but the TENT branch only special-cases `"tcp"`. `"efa"` / `"ascend"` do not pin those transports. On `USE_EFA` / `USE_CXI` Python builds, `initialize` still calls `installTransport()` after init; under TENT that returns `nullptr` and `initialize` returns `-1`. #4122 is classic TE Ascend Direct selection, not this shim item.
- **P1-sync-status.** `transferSync` still retries `numContexts()+1` times; under TENT `numContexts()` is hardcoded `1`. The poll loop handles `COMPLETED` / `FAILED` / `TIMEOUT` only — not `CANCELED` — and does not evict the cached handle on poll failure.
- **P1-install-transport.** Added from @chlins (2026-09-14). The TENT branch logs `"installTransport not used by TENT"` and returns `nullptr`. Classic contract: `nullptr` means install failed. Store already skips this via `isUsingTent()` (#2596). C / Go (`transfer_engine_c.h`) and EFA/CXI Python do not. Proposed fix A (TENT returns a non-null sentinel; in-tree callers only null-check) is preferred over gating every caller (B) or fixing only the C shim (C). Waiting on TENT owners (@alogfans) before a PR. R

items.title: [RFC]: [AI QoS] Per-engine Ascend QoS and priority lanes
items.author: A-zhudong
items.body_excerpt:
## Changes proposed

Enable applications to select different Ascend transfer priorities within one process. Each priority lane owns an independently configured engine, allowing requests to select a lane without changing process-wide environment variables.

Proposed changes:

- Add explicit per-engine Ascend resource configuration through a six-argument `TransferEngine::init` overload and a corresponding Python initialization API. Preserve existing four- and five-argument calls.
- Preserve explicit per-engine resource overrides when loading TENT configuration.
- Provide Python priority-lane helpers for Store and PD transfers, including memory registration, failure cleanup, and engine lifecycle management.
- Keep Store lanes in a shared key space while retaining existing tenant, device, and replica settings.

This provides the backend for request-level KV transfer priority in vLLM-Ascend. Independently configured engines allow priorities to coexist while reusing the existing Ascend transport implementation.

Validation includes 22 CPU configuration tests, two initialization tests, one Store TCP test, TENT ON / Ascend Direct ON builds, native import and clean-exit probes, and A5 Store, PD, and layerwise integration tests.

Feedback is welcome on the per-engine initialization API and the placement of reusable priority-lane helpers in the Python package.

## Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Searched relevant issues and reviewed the project documentation.

items.title: [inductor] Attention-shaped pattern rewrite ignores the softmax dim, silently computing attention over the last axis
items.author: laolvfan
items.body_excerpt:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

An attention-shaped chain whose softmax is taken over a **non-last** dimension is
rewritten by the post-grad pattern matcher as if the softmax were over the last
dimension. The compiled function silently returns the result of a *different*
computation — no error, no warning, no graph break.

```python
import torch, torch.nn as nn

class M(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, sm_dim):
        super().__init__()
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(0.23)
        self.sm_dim = sm_dim
    def forward(self, q, k, v):
        qk = torch.matmul(q, k.transpose(-2, -1))
        s = qk.div(128)
        s = torch.softmax(s, dim=self.sm_dim)   # dim=0, NOT the last dim
        s = self.dropout(s)
        return s.matmul(v)

torch.manual_seed(0)
q, k, v = torch.randn(4,4,2,8), torch.randn(4,4,3,8), torch.randn(4,4,3,8)

def ev(m):
    m.train(False)
    with torch.no_grad():
        return m(q, k, v)

def cp(m):
    m.train(False); torch._dynamo.reset()
    with torch.no_grad():
        return torch.compile(m, backend="inductor")(q, k, v)

rel = lambda a, b: ((a-b).abs().max() / a.abs().max()).item()

print(rel(ev(M(0)),  cp(M(0))))    # 0.3462      eager vs compiled, dim=0
print(rel(cp(M(0)),  ev(M(-1))))   # 6.5e-08     compiled(dim=0) == eager(dim=-1)
```

### The compiled `dim=0` model computes the `dim=-1` model

The second number is the point: the compiled output of the `dim=0` model is
numerically identical to the **eager output of the `dim=-1` model**, so the
rewrite has silently replaced the user's softmax axis with the last axis.

### It is the pattern matcher

Disabling the pattern matcher removes the divergence entirely, and a model that
really does use `dim=-1` is unaffected:

| configuration | max relative diff (eager vs compiled) |
|---|---|
| `softmax(dim=0)`, `pattern_matcher=True` | **8.72** (shapes `(50,50,4,64)`) / **0.346** (shapes `(4,4,2,8)`) |
| `softmax(dim=0)`, `pattern_matcher=False` | 7.0e-08 |
| `softmax(dim=-1)`, `pattern_matcher=True` | 1.7e-07 |

```python
import torch._inductor.config as cfg
cfg.pattern_matcher = False   # divergence disappears
```

`nn.Dropout` is in eval mode throughout (`m.train(False)`), so it is an identity
and the comparison is deterministic — the eager output is bit-stable over 200
repeated runs.

### Note on related reports

This is a different root cause from #195320 (which is about a permuted `K` being
bound as if it were `key.transpose(-2,-1)`). Here `k.transpose(-2, -1)` is the
canonical form and the operands are bound correctly; the only mismatched
attribute is the softmax dimension, which the rewrite does not check.

### Versions

Reproduced on `2.14.0+cpu`, CPU, inductor backend.

items.title: [Core] Cluster scheduling degrades under specific load
items.author: leviska
items.body_excerpt:
### What happened + What you expected to happen

**Intro**

We've encountered this issue multiple times, but could not determine the cause
First we encountered when we've spawned tasks without backpressure - we have quite large nodes for head and workers, so it wasnt the OOM, but the cluster just could not schedule the tasks
We've added backpressure after that, and it help a lot - but still, once every while the cluster degraded
Finally I was able to capture the degradation and asked Claude to help with the debugging, and here's it's report on the issue

**Summary:** One raylet can get stuck for hours with thousands of leases in `num_waiting_for_remote_node_resources` while every other node in the cluster is idle. The trigger is a workload that creates many scheduling classes, e.g. code that calls `ray.remote(fn)` on every submission, so every task gets a fresh random `function_hash`. Two things combine:

1. A scheduling pass on the raylet costs time proportional to the **square** of the number of queued scheduling classes.
2. The raylet runs a **full scheduling pass for every resource-view sync message** it receives.

Once one pass takes more than about a second, the raylet can no longer keep up with incoming sync messages. Its view of the cluster freezes, and it believes every other node is full. It neither runs nor spills back the leases queued on it. Workers it starts then time out during registration, which makes it worse. The node recovers only after the backlog drains or the submitting jobs end, which can take many hours.

**Expected:** a raylet with idle remote nodes in the cluster should spill those leases back within seconds, however many scheduling classes exist.

**Observed** (30 worker nodes × 80 CPU / 200 GiB, Ray 2.55.0):

- Autoscaler status showed 40/2400 CPU in use and dozens of pending demands that never got scheduled.
- All pending leases were on a single raylet. Its state dump:
  ```
  Grant queue length: 7180
  num_waiting_for_remote_node_resources: 7162
  ```
  Every other raylet reported empty queues and 80/80 CPU, 200/200 GiB available.
- That raylet's cluster view had been **frozen for ~16 h**. It still showed 0 GiB memory free on nodes that had been completely idle for hours.
- `scheduling_class_util.cc: More than 408043 types of tasks seen` on that node; 574k on the head node.
- Event stats over a 31-minute window on the affected raylet:
  - `NodeManager.ScheduleAndGrantLeases`: ~1.6 s per call
  - `RaySyncer.BroadcastMessage`: ~1.4 s per call. Each received message triggers a scheduling pass.
  - Main event loop queueing delay up to ~290 s
- It processed ~3.4k sync messages in 15 h; a healthy raylet in the same cluster processed ~271k.
- Worker registration timed out repeatedly. There were 237 `Some workers of the worker process(...) have not registered within the timeout` in one hour, followed by `Received a register request from an unknown worker`.
- `There are more than 100 scheduling classes. Some resource loads may not be reported to the autoscaler.` (173k times), so the autoscaler's pending demands showed only a fraction of the real backlog.

The code paths below are unchanged in **2.59.0**.

### Root cause (code pointers, 2.59.0)

1. **A scheduling pass is quadratic in the number of scheduling classes.**
   In `LocalLeaseManager::GrantScheduledLeasesToWorkers` (`local_lease_manager.cc`), the fair-share block runs once per scheduling class. Each time it re-iterates all of `leases_to_grant_` to compute `num_classes_with_cpu` / `total_cpu_requests_`, and all of `info_by_sched_cls_` to compute `total_cpu_granted_leases`. With ~7k queued classes that's tens of millions of iterations per pass. (This attribution comes from reading the code plus the event stats above; I haven't captured a `perf` profile yet.)

2. **One scheduling pass per sync message.**
   `NodeManager::ConsumeSyncMessage` calls `cluster_lease_manager_.ScheduleAndGrantLeases()` for every RESOURCE_VIEW message it receives. Once a pass is expensive, processing sync messages becomes the bottleneck, and the cluster view goes stale.

3. **The scheduling-class table never shrinks** (`SchedulingClassToIds::GetSchedulingClass`, `TODO(ekl) we might want to try cleaning up task types`). Every `ray.remote(fn)` call gets `uuid4()` as its function hash (`remote_function.py`, `PythonFunctionDescriptor.from_function(self._function, self._uuid)`), so per-call `ray.remote` creates an unbounded number of classes.

**Related, smaller issue: dead and unknown nodes come back into raylet views.** `ConsumeSyncMessage` → `SetNodeLabels` / `ResourceCreateUpdated` → `UpdateResourceCapacity` adds any node ID it hasn't seen, without checking that the GCS knows it as alive. We saw:
- 31 node IDs from a previous cluster session. Old raylets reconnected to a restarted GCS before failing the cluster-ID check, and those IDs now sit in every raylet's view with frozen usage.
- A node marked dead by health check, re-added by a sync message that arrived after its death notification.

These entries are skipped when choosing a node, so they don't cause the stall. They do make every scheduling decision scan more nodes, and they make state dumps misleading.

### Suggested fixes

1. **Run one scheduling pass for a burst of sync messages, not one per message.** This decouples view freshness from scheduling cost and breaks the feedback loop:
   ```cpp
   void NodeManager::ScheduleAndGrantLeasesCoalesced() {
     if (schedule_pass_posted_) return;
     schedule_pass_posted_ = true;
     io_service_.post([this] {
       schedule_pass_posted_ = false;
       cluster_lease_manager_.ScheduleAndGrantLeases();
     }, "NodeManager.ScheduleAndGrantLeasesCoalesced");
   }
   // ConsumeSyncMessage:
   if (capacity_updated || usage_update) ScheduleAndGrantLeasesCoalesced();
   ```
   The syncer already runs on the main `io_service_`, so this stays single-threaded.

2. **Make the fair-share computation linear per pass.** Compute `num_classes_with_

items.title: [Bug] GLM-5.3-Flash (DSA): HiCache host-tier load-back corrupts generation even without speculative decoding — dropped tool calls, degenerate repetition loops (8×H100, TP8)
items.author: d3lavar
items.body_excerpt:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

On GLM-5.3-Flash (packed DSA KV / `DSATokenToKVPool`, `--attention-backend dsa`), enabling HiCache host offload (`--hicache-size` / `--hicache-ratio`) corrupts generation for requests whose prefix round-trips through the host tier (device → host → device). **Speculative decoding is not required — the corruption reproduces with EAGLE/MTP fully disabled; HiCache alone is broken.** Three failure signatures, all appearing only after host load-back:

1. **Tool calls silently dropped** — `finish_reason=stop`, `tool_calls=null`, with a prose "answer" that often hallucinates the tool output, even though the model's reasoning explicitly announces the call.
2. **Degenerate repetition loops / broken token sequences** — output gets stuck repeating filler tokens from the system prompt (or a single phrase) until `max_tokens` truncation.

**Isolation on the same production 8×H100 node, same workload (2026-09-04):**

| HiCache (`--hicache-ratio 2 --hicache-size 140`) | EAGLE/MTP | Result |
|---|---|---|
| ON | ON | **corrupted** — signatures 1–3 |
| ON | **OFF** | **still corrupted** — intermittent: byte-identical warm replays mostly pass, but individual host load-back runs drop tool calls or loop (1 of 6 warm replays broken in one window, 4/4 post-eviction replays broken in another) |
| OFF (device radix only) | ON | clean — 5/5 on the originally broken session |

The corruption is **intermittent** on host load-back: a byte-identical replay succeeds several times in a row, then a later identical replay corrupts (see `warm1/warm2/warm3` below). The fault lives in the **HiCache host-tier load-back path itself**; EAGLE adds its own draft-state sensitivity on top (#28895) but is not required for the bug.

### Setup

- **Hardware:** 8× NVIDIA H100 (single node), TP8 / DP1 / EP8
- **Image:** [`lmsysorg/sglang:glm-5.3-flash`](https://hub.docker.com/r/lmsysorg/sglang) — build of PR #36507 (branch `xinyuan/glm-5.3-flash-support`), with #37925 (`glm53` tool-call parser) and #37534 (packed-DSA HiCache host-row width fix) cherry-picked. The corruption persists with both, so #37534 is not sufficient for the spec-decode combination.
- **Launch (broken config), flags confirmed verbatim from `/server_info`:**

  ```bash
  python -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path glm-5.3-flash \
    --tp-size 8 --dp-size 1 --ep-size 8 \
    --attention-backend dsa \
    --page-size 64 \
    --tool-call-parser glm53 --reasoning-parser glm45 \
    --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 16384 \
    --mem-fraction-static 0.7 --max-running-requests 48 \
    --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
    --speculative-num-steps 5 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
    --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 --speculative-adaptive \
    --hicache-ratio 2 --hicache-size 140 \
    --hicache-write-policy write_through \
    --hicache-mem-layout page-first-direct \
    --hicache-io-backend direct
  ```

  Removing the `--hicache-*` flags removes the corruption. Disabling EAGLE does **not** — with HiCache on, generation still corrupts without speculative decoding but later, cannot determine the moment yet.
- **Pressure conditions:** device KV pool ~93% used (~601K tokens), host pool LRU ~99.9% full — prefixes actively evict to host and load back between turns.
- **Workload:** agentic client, 47 tools, streaming, OpenAI-style history, 100K–230K-token prompts.

### Evidence (verbatim excerpts from the script above, HiCache ON, glm53 parser + #37534 build; observed with EAGLE both ON and OFF)

Phase 1 (device radix hits) is mostly healthy, but even the first warm window already drops calls intermittently:

```text
cold-180K    dt=27.3s  prompt=225686  cached=128     finish=tool_calls  tools=['bash']
warm1-180K   dt= 1.7s  prompt=225686  cached=225664  finish=tool_calls  tools=['bash']
warm2-180K   dt= 1.1s  prompt=225686  cached=225664  finish=stop        tools=[]      <- BROKEN
warm3-180K   dt= 1.5s  prompt=225686  cached=225664  finish=tool_calls  tools=['bash']
```

`warm2-180K` content — the model hallucinates the tool result instead of calling the tool:

```text
Here's the output from running the command:

```
hello-acceptance
```
```

Phase 3 (same byte-identical prompts after eviction, i.e. served from HiCache host load-back) — tool-call drops plus degenerate repetition loops:

```text
replay1-60K   dt= 0.8s  cached=75328   finish=stop          tools=[]  tail: "echo hello-acceptance"
replay2-60K   dt=33.0s  cached=75328   finish=length(2000)  tools=[]  tail: "oscar oscar oscar oscar oscar oscar 999999999
juliet juliet juliet jul"
replay1-180K  dt=28.0s  cached=225664  finish=length(2000)  tools=[]  tail: "tice the notice the notice the notice the notice ..."
replay2-180K  dt=58.2s  cached=225664  finish=length(2000)  tools=[]
```

`oscar`/`juliet` are random filler words from the system prompt — the model is regurgitating corrupted prefill tokens. Phase 2 (eviction pressure, ~2.2M tokens vs ~601K device pool)

For comparison: with HiCache disabled (device radix only) — clean, including warm replays and post-eviction replays; with EAGLE disabled but HiCache on — corruption is still observed on host load-back (tool-call drops and repetition loops, as above).

### Notes on root cause (hypothesis)

Host-tier backup/load-back corrupts the packed DSA KV rows themselves (`DSATokenToKVPool`): after a device → host → device round-trip the prefill KV no longer matches what the original token sequence produced, so the model "misreads its own history" — no valid tool call, confabulated r

items.title: `torch.compile` (inductor) — `interpolate(mode='nearest')` resamples a spatial dimension whose size is unchanged, disagreeing with eager
items.author: tinywisdom
items.body_excerpt:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

`F.interpolate(x, scale_factor=..., mode='nearest')` disagrees between eager and
`torch.compile` (inductor) when a `scale_factor` is non-integer but the resulting output size
equals the input size for that dimension. Eager treats such an **unchanged spatial dimension as
identity** (source index = destination index, no resampling); the compiled lowering still applies
the user-provided non-unit scale factor and resamples that dimension, selecting different source
pixels. Same output shape, different values, no error.

## Minimal repro

```python
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

# H: 3 -> floor(3*1.3)=3 (UNCHANGED) with a non-unit scale;  W: 4 -> floor(4*1.5)=6 (changed)
x = torch.arange(12, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(1, 1, 3, 4)   # CPU, float32

def fn(z):
    return F.interpolate(z, scale_factor=(1.3, 1.5), mode='nearest')

e = fn(x)
c = torch.compile(fn, backend="inductor")(x)

# height source-row mapping (first column of each output row):
print([int(e[0, 0, i, 0]) // 4 for i in range(3)])   # eager:    [0, 1, 2]  (unchanged dim -> identity)
print([int(c[0, 0, i, 0]) // 4 for i in range(3)])   # compiled: [0, 0, 1]  (resampled with scale 1.3)
print(torch.equal(e, c))                              # False
```

## Expected vs actual

- **Expected**: compiled matches eager — a dimension whose output size equals its input size is
  passed through unchanged (identity), so the height rows map [0, 1, 2].
- **Actual**: inductor resamples the unchanged height dimension using the raw `scale_factor=1.3`,
  mapping rows [0, 0, 1] — different pixels, silently.

## Scope (observed, CPU and CUDA identical)

| dim | input→output | scale | eager vs compiled |
|---|---|---|---|
| output size **==** input size | 3→3 | 1.3 | **DIFF** (eager identity, compiled resamples) |
| output size **==** input size | 4→4 | 1.2 | **DIFF** |
| output size changes | 3→6 | 2.0 | same |
| output size changes (shrink) | 3→2 | 0.7 | same |

Only the "unchanged size + non-unit scale" case diverges; dimensions that actually change size
agree. Reproduces on both CPU and CUDA (eager's equal-size shortcut is device-independent).

### Versions

```
PyTorch version: 2.15.0a0+gite67e43b
Is debug build: True
CUDA used to build PyTorch: 12.6
ROCM used to build PyTorch: N/A

OS: Ubuntu 22.04.4 LTS (x86_64)
GCC version: (Ubuntu 12.3.0-1ubuntu1~22.04.3) 12.3.0
Clang version: 17.0.6
CMake version: version 4.0.0
Libc version: glibc-2.35

Python version: 3.12.13 | packaged by conda-forge (64-bit runtime)
Python platform: Linux-6.8.0-138-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.35
Is CUDA available: True
CUDA runtime version: 12.6.20
GPU 0: NVIDIA RTX A6000
Nvidia driver version: 580.82.07
cuDNN version: 9.3.0

[pip3] numpy==2.3.5
[pip3] torch==2.15.0a0+gite67e43b
[pip3] triton==3.7.1
```

items.title: `torch.compile channel_shuffle identity shortcut preserves non-contiguous strides unlike eager CUDA, causing downstream view to fail`
items.author: tinywisdom
items.body_excerpt:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

A non-contiguous CUDA tensor passed through `torch.channel_shuffle(x, 1)` and then a legal `.view(...)` works in eager but crashes under `torch.compile` on **all** backends (`eager`, `aot_eager`, `inductor`) during fake-tensor propagation. Since `backend="eager"` (Dynamo + fake tensor, no Inductor codegen) already crashes, the fault is in the shared ref/decomposition (meta) layer, not Inductor.

```python
import torch
x = torch.randn(1,4,2,2,device='cuda').permute(0,3,1,2)   # (1,2,4,2), strides (16,1,4,2), non-contiguous
def fn(x): return torch.channel_shuffle(x, 1).view(x.size(0), -1)

fn(x)                                              # eager:    (1,16), ok
torch.compile(fn, backend="eager")(x)              # TorchRuntimeError: RuntimeError when making fake tensor call: view(...)
torch.compile(fn, backend="aot_eager")(x)          # same
torch.compile(fn, backend="inductor")(x)           # same
```

**Root cause.** The `channel_shuffle` reference (`torch/_refs/nn/functional/__init__.py`, `@register_decomposition(aten.channel_shuffle)`) short-circuits to `return input.view(input.shape)` for `device_hint(input) == "cuda" and (groups == 1 or groups == c)`, which **preserves the input's non-contiguous strides**. The real path (and eager CUDA `math_channel_shuffle`) ends in `.contiguous()`, producing a contiguous result. For a non-contiguous input the identity `view(input.shape)` succeeds but returns a non-contiguous alias, whereas eager returns a contiguous tensor — so the user's subsequent legal `.view()` fails only under compile.

**Expected.** Compiled `channel_shuffle` should match eager's layout (contiguous for this input), so the downstream `.view()` succeeds as it does in eager.

**Related but distinct.** Related to #198424/#199139, but that fixes `native_channel_shuffle`'s first `view({b, groups, oc, -1})`; this fails at a *different* shortcut (`view(input.shape)` in the ref) and is **not** fixed by replacing `native_channel_shuffle`'s first view with reshape. Also related to #194561, which only re-gates the identity shortcut (CPU vs non-CPU), leaves CUDA unchanged, and assumes `.contiguous()` is a no-op for these group counts — which does not hold for non-contiguous input.

### Versions

```
PyTorch version: 2.15.0a0+git1a080e5
Is debug build: True
CUDA used to build PyTorch: 12.6
ROCM used to build PyTorch: N/A

OS: Ubuntu 22.04.4 LTS (x86_64)
GCC version: (Ubuntu 12.3.0-1ubuntu1~22.04.3) 12.3.0
Clang version: 17.0.6
CMake version: version 4.0.0
Libc version: glibc-2.35

items.title: [Testing] Triage of red tests that still need a fix (90-day sweep)
items.author: bolubo
items.body_excerpt:
## Summary

A 90 day sweep of the Actions history (2026-06-26 to 2026-09-25) turned up 455 failed runs. Most of them are already fixed, tied to a PR branch that was still iterating, or environmental. This issue is about what is left: tests that are still going red and do not have a fix, with enough evidence attached that someone can pick one up without redoing the whole investigation.

Two of the items reproduce locally on main today (A). Four more keep showing up in CI across branches, where the mechanism is narrowed down but there is no local repro yet (B). The appendices cover the one-off flakes and the families that are already fixed, so nobody has to dig through them again.

The coverage side already has tracking issues (#2637, #2708, #2737); this list is a different axis, tests that are failing right now.

If you want to take one, please comment on the item first so two people do not end up on the same thing, and link the PR here when it is up. Small focused PRs are the easiest to review.

## Items

- [ ] A1. Gateway rate limiter windows follow the wall clock, and three tests flake on the bucket boundary.
- [ ] A2. Two tests have been skipped since April 2025, and both pass when re-enabled.
- [ ] B1. The SLO queue spec times out on the release path.
- [ ] B2. The RoleSet topology spec hits a 409 conflict.
- [ ] B3. Batch e2e: a restored job does not reach `completed` within the 60s budget.
- [ ] B4. The planner unit test hangs and trips the 10 minute package timeout.

Grading:

- A: reproduced locally on main (`544204ae`), with a measured failure rate over repeated runs.
- B: repeated red in CI on main or across branches; no local repro yet.
- Watch: seen once; kept for reference.
- Fixed: already covered by a merged PR; do not re-triage.

## A. Reproduced locally on main

### A1. Gateway rate limiter windows follow the wall clock

`pkg/plugins/gateway/ratelimiter/redis.go:77` builds the counter key as `name:key:<unix/window % 64>`, so the counter changes on wall-clock bucket boundaries. A pair of calls that should share one window can land in two buckets instead, and the second call gets a fresh counter and is admitted. The TTL side is already anchored to the first write (`incrAndExpireScript`), so the key rotation is the remaining race.

- Affected tests: `pkg/plugins/gateway/replica_rps_test.go:96` (`TestModelReplicaRPS_Half_AllowsOneRequestEveryTwoSeconds`), `pkg/plugins/gateway/replica_inflight_test.go:335` (`TestHandleRequestBody_ReplicaInflightCoexistsWithReplicaRPS`), and `pkg/plugins/gateway/gateway_ratelimit_test.go:270` (`TestEnforceModelRPS_RejectDoesNotPostponeNextWindow`, added with #2726).
- How often it fails on main (one process per run, `-count=1`): 3 red in 100 runs for the first pair, 14 red in 450 runs for the third test, so roughly one run in thirty. The failure messages are "a second request within the same 2s window should be rejected" and "immediate retry should be rejected by the still-open window".
- CI hit: [run 35654425095, job 106514390571](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/actions/runs/35654425095/job/106514390571), Go Race Tests on 09-21, same assertion at `gateway_ratelimit_test.go:270`.
- Repro: `for i in $(seq 1 50); do go test ./pkg/plugins/gateway -run 'TestModelReplicaRPS_Half_AllowsOneRequestEveryTwoSeconds|TestHandleRequestBody_ReplicaInflightCoexistsWithReplicaRPS' -count=1; done`
- Two ways to fix it, and this is a real tradeoff: (1) anchor the window at the first write so every call in the same window computes the same key, which is what the tests already assume, at the cost of changing behavior at bucket boundaries; or (2) keep the wall-clock bucket and make the tests independent of it by injecting the clock, which is a smaller change but leaves the boundary burst in the product.

### A2. Two tests skipped since April 2025

- `pkg/utils/prefixcacheindexer/tree_test.go:33` (`Test_LPRadixCacheE2E`) and `:71` (`Test_RadixMatchPrefix`) have carried `t.SkipNow()` since `d546795a` (#933, April 2025). Removing the two lines makes both pass locally, in under 0.1s including subtests.
- `apps/console/api/resource_manager/provider/kubernetes/catalog_test.go:33` skips unconditionally with `t.Skip("skip for now")`, which also makes the kubeconfig checks below it dead code. Either delete the line or gate it on the environment with a stated reason.
- Repro: `go test ./pkg/utils/prefixcacheindexer -run 'Test_LPRadixCacheE2E|Test_RadixMatchPrefix' -v`

## B. Repeated red in CI, no local repro yet

### B1. SLO queue spec times out on the release path

- `pkg/plugins/gateway/algorithms/slo_test.go:253` ("Queue router should be blocked and released successfully") fails with `context deadline exceeded` at `:270`, after the 10s per spec budget.
- Hits since June: 06-28 `exclusive_topology`, 08-17 `route-dev` and `feat/align-job-time-window`, 09-05 `ui-aiconfigurator`, 09-09 `feat-pd-hybrid-cache-load`, 09-12 `roshpr/feat-stormservice-pooled-scale`, 09-20 `andreafeat/disable-gateway-rate-limiting` (race job). #2335 reported this spec in June and was closed after #2328 and #2353 merged, but it still recurs.
- A 150 run local loop is green, so it needs a CI style repro first. Fixing it likely means either making the assertion event driven or making the fixed wait budget explicit and generous.

### B2. RoleSet topology spec hits a 409 conflict

- `test/integration/controller/roleset_test.go:1062` ("applies topology policy updates only to newly created pods") fails at `:1118` with `Operation cannot be fulfilled on rolesets... the object has been modified; please apply your changes to the latest version and try again`. Latest hit: [35814726502](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/actions/runs/35814726502) on main, 09-23, 89 of 90 specs passed. Two more on 08-04.
- The spec updates the RoleSet while a reconcile is in flight, so `retry.RetryOnConflict` around the update (or `Eventually`) should close the race. Test side, no product change expected.

### B3. Ba
